record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.context_brief: Well-posedness for delayed consumer-resource PDE system
record.original_question: For the delayed consumer-resource system ∂_t u = d22 u_xx − d21 ∂_x(u ∂_x v_τ) + f(u,v) and ∂_t v = d11 v_xx + g(u,v), where consumers move up the gradient of the resource density from τ time units in the past, under what conditions does a unique solution exist with homogeneous Neumann boundary data, and what changes in higher spatial dimensions?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 27. Under what conditions does a unique solution exist solving problem (2.24) subject to homogeneous Neumann boundary data? What about in higher spatial dimensions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the delayed consumer–resource reaction–diffusion–advection system on a bounded smooth domain Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ (initially n = 1, say Ω = (a,b)):

  ∂ₜ u(x,t) = d₂₂ Δu(x,t) − d₂₁ ∇·(u(x,t) ∇v(x,t−τ)) + f(u(x,t), v(x,t)),
  ∂ₜ v(x,t) = d₁₁ Δv(x,t) + g(u(x,t), v(x,t)),
   (x,t) ∈ Ω × (0,∞),

where u(x,t) ≥ 0 denotes the consumer density, v(x,t) ≥ 0 denotes the resource density, d₁₁, d₂₂ > 0 are diffusion coefficients, d₂₁ > 0 is an advection (taxis) coefficient, and τ > 0 is a memory delay so that consumers move up the gradient of the resource density evaluated τ time units in the past. The reaction terms f, g : ℝ₊² → ℝ are smooth (e.g. of Lotka–Volterra or Holling type). The system is supplemented with homogeneous Neumann (zero-flux) boundary conditions

  ∂ν u = 0,  ∂ν v = 0  on ∂Ω × (0,∞),

and with initial history data u(x,0) = u₀(x) and v(x,t) = v₀(x,t) for (x,t) ∈ Ω × [−τ, 0], in appropriate function spaces.

Problem. Determine sufficient conditions on the parameters (d₁₁, d₂₂, d₂₁, τ), the nonlinearities (f, g), and the initial data (u₀, v₀) under which the above initial–boundary value problem admits a unique (classical or weak) global-in-time nonnegative solution. Moreover, establish the analogous well-posedness theory when the spatial domain Ω is taken in higher dimensions n ≥ 2, identifying any additional smallness, regularity, or structural assumptions that become necessary.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent works have addressed well-posedness for closely related cognitive consumer–resource models with nonlocal perception and spatial memory. In particular, a Journal of Nonlinear Science paper by Song–Wang–Wang treats the cognitive consumer–resource system with nonlocal perception, and a 2025 paper in Mathematical Methods in the Applied Sciences obtains a unique globally Hölder continuous weak solution for a diffusive resource–consumer model with nonlocal memory usage. A 2025/2026 Journal of Nonlinear Science paper studies well-posedness, stability, and bifurcation for a coupled nonlocal PDE–ODE system with spatial memory. These results give partial answers, primarily in one spatial dimension or under nonlocal averaging of the delayed gradient; a complete well-posedness theory for the pointwise-delayed taxis system in higher dimensions does not appear fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Cognitive Consumer-Resource Spatiotemporal Dynamics with Nonlocal Perception
status_evidence.snippet: Studies a cognitive consumer–resource model incorporating nonlocal perception, establishing existence/uniqueness results in this related setting.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on well-posedness for the related nonlocal-perception consumer–resource model.

status_evidence.title: Diffusive Resource–Consumer Dynamics With the Simplest Learning Mechanism and Nonlocal Memory Usage
status_evidence.snippet: Obtains a unique globally Hölder continuous weak solution for a diffusive resource–consumer model with nonlocal memory usage, resolving an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Provides well-posedness for a closely related delayed/memory consumer–resource model.

status_evidence.title: Dynamics of a Coupled Nonlocal PDE-ODE System with Spatial Memory: Well-Posedness, Stability, and Bifurcation Analysis
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes well-posedness, stability and bifurcation analysis for a coupled nonlocal PDE–ODE system with spatial memory.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial well-posedness progress on related delayed/memory models.
